title: US midterms trigger Wall Street rout: How AI sell-off is spreading beyond Big Tech to riskier stocks

title: US midterm outcome mildly positive for gold, but Fed risks persist: Analyst
excerpt: Praveen Singh of Mirae Asset Sharekhan said that gold's upside could remain constrained by expectations of further Fed tightening, particularly if US economic data remain firm or oil prices rebound.

ai.title_te: US మిడ్టర్మ్ ఎన్నికల ఫలితాలు గోల్డ్‌కు కొంత సహకారం, కానీ Fed ప్రభావం కొనసాగుతోంది
ai.summary: Mirae Asset Sharekhan విశ్లేషకుడు ప్రవీణ్ సింగ్ ప్రకారం, US మిడ్టర్మ్ ఎన్నికల ఫలితాలు గోల్డ్ ధరలకు కొంతవరకు సానుకూలంగా ఉన్నాయి. అయితే, US ఆర్థిక డేటా బలంగా ఉంటే లేదా క్రూడ్ ఆయిల్ ధరలు పెరిగితే, Fed మరింత రిట్‌రెంట్ (tightening) చేసే అవకాశం ఉంది, దీనివల్ల గోల్డ్ పెరుగుదల పరిమితంగా ఉండవచ్చు.

title: India bonds emerge as top Asian performers as oil, Treasury yields decline
excerpt: This week, Indian government bonds saw a positive trend following a Democratic win in the U.S. midterm elections. The reduction in oil prices and Treasury yields eased rupee pressure, boosting investor confidence. The benchmark bond yield improved significantly, declining by approximately 22 basis points. Furthermore, the surge in foreign investments into Indian bonds marked a notable high since July, leading to enhanced overall market sentiment.

title: Rupee falls 9 paise to 94.50 against US dollar in early trade
excerpt: In early trading on Friday, the rupee slipped by 9 paise to reach 94.50 against the US dollar, driven by a robust dollar and surging crude oil prices. After a brief bounce-back, it peaked at 94.36. The domestic equity market exhibited mixed performance, with Sensex rising yet Nifty falling. Notably, Foreign Institutional Investors remained active, purchasing substantial equities, bolstering market optimism.

title: India's foreign exchange reserves drop by $2.69 billion to $717 billion
excerpt:
India's forex reserves dropped by USD 2.691 billion to USD 717.056 billion during the week ended October 30, the RBI said on Friday.
In the previous week, the forex kitty had reduced by USD 1.269 billion to USD 719.748 billion.
The reserves had touched an all-time high of USD 785.706 billion during the week ended September 4, driven by a heavy flow of currency as part of a special concessional swap for deposits from the diaspora through which banks raised a record USD 133 billion, but have been on a decline ever since.
Experts attribute this decline to the deployment of the FCNR(B) resources and also to currency defence put up by RBI through dollar sales.

ai.impact_reason_te: గవర్నమెంట్ బాండ్ యీల్డ్స్ స్థిరంగా ఉండటం వల్ల బ్యాంకులు కొత్త బాండ్లను కొనుగోలు చేసినప్పుడు వాటి యీల్డ్ స్ప్రెడ్ (Yield Spread) తగ్గదు. దీనివల్ల బ్యాంకుల నికర ఆదాయం (Net Interest Income)పై ప్రతికూల ప్రభావం తగ్గుతుంది.
